newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF MARSEILLE PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF MARSEILLE PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Marseille players most likely to play in Saturday's French first division match against Monaco at the Louis II stadium.

Andreas Koepke, goalkeeper, age 33. A member of Germany's European championship-winning side last year, he has been a tower of strength during a troublesome settling-in period for Marseille in their first season back in the top flight. He joined the club after his transfer to Barcelona fell through. In doubt with calf injury.
Jerome Alonzo, goalkeeper, 24. Promotion side's goalkeeper, he is now Koepke's reserve and could play if the German is unfit.
Alberto Malusci, defender, 24. Signed from Fiorentina after helping them win the Italian Cup last season. Looked on his way to AC Milan at one time but was out for a long period due to injury.

Christophe Galtier, defender, 30. Former French under-21 international who returned to Marseille, his first club, in 1995 after playing for Lille, Toulouse, Angers and Nimes. Played in Marseille's 1986 and 1987 French Cup final sides.
Chris Makin, defender, 23. Englishman who joined Marseille from Oldham Athletic this season as a second string player but has played himself into the first team.

Hamada Jambay, defender, 21. Born in the Comoros Islands, he rose through the club's youth ranks after joining at the age of eight. A first team regular for two seasons. Has scored some spectacular long range goals.

Jean-Christophe Marquet, defender, 22 (23 on Monday). regular left back in promotion side following season on loan at Cannes under Luis Fernandez, but only recently won back place in team after leg surgery in the off-season.

Bernard Ferrer, midfielder, 33. After helping Marseille win promotion, has been useful substitute in defensive positions this season. Began career at Auxerre where he spent seven seasons under Guy Roux.

Eric Roy, midfielder, 29. Signed from Lyon this season to help strengthen team promoted from the second division. He has been one of the steadiest of the new signings. Returns from one-match suspension.
Olivier Echouafni, midfielder, 24. Began his career at Monaco. Dubbed the "washing machine" by coach Gerard Gili for his capacity to recycle Marseille's midfield play.

Yordan Lechkov, midfielder, 29. Bulgarian international who reached heights by helping his country to the 1994 World Cup semifinals, but struggled to keep a first team place at Marseille. Returns from a one-match suspension.

Xavier Gravelaine, forward, 28. Capped four times by France, much-travelled striker who joined from Guingamp this season after two spells with Paris St Germain. Team's top scorer with 13 league goals.
Marc Libbra, forward, 24. Scored 14 goals (second only to Irishman Tony Cascarino's 30) during promotion season. His tally this season stands at eight league goals.
